title: Fortis Noida launches lung failure clinic for advanced respiratory disease management and transplant care

contentHtml:
Specialised multidisciplinary care for advanced lung diseases, including transplant evaluation, pulmonary rehabilitation and structured follow-ups

Fortis Hospital Noida has launched a dedicated lung failure clinic aimed at providing structured assessment and care for patients suffering from advanced and end-stage lung disease. The clinic will focus on facilitating early identification and evaluation of patients who may need lung transplantation and provide access to specialised respiratory care through a multidisciplinary approach.

The clinic will be led by Dr Rahul Sharma, Director, Department of Pulmonary Medicine and Critical Care, Fortis Hospital, Noida, along with Dr Govini Balasubramani, Director & HOD – Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Gleneagles Hospitals, Chennai (A Fortis Network Hospital).

It will provide structured assessment and care for patients with advanced respiratory conditions, including interstitial lung diseases (ILD), pulmonary fibrosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and other progressive lung conditions. Services will include medical optimisation, counselling on available treatment options and evaluation for lung transplantation where clinically appropriate. For potential transplant candidates, the clinic will facilitate further assessment and referral to an appropriately authorised transplant centre. It will also support structured post-transplant follow-up, including monitoring for complications, in coordination with the treating transplant team. A multidisciplinary team comprising pulmonologists, thoracic surgeons, transplant specialists, intensivists and allied healthcare professionals will guide care according to each patient’s clinical needs.

Dr Balasubramani said, “We are witnessing a steady rise in patients with advanced lung diseases, driven by multiple factors including air pollution, tobacco exposure, occupational hazards, infections and an ageing population. Unfortunately, many patients reach us only when their lung function has deteriorated significantly. Early diagnosis, timely referral and specialised multidisciplinary care are critical to slowing disease progression and improving outcomes. The Lung Failure Clinic has been established to bridge this gap by providing comprehensive evaluation, optimisation of medical therapy, pulmonary rehabilitation and, where appropriate, timely assessment for lung transplantation.”

Dr Sharma said, “Patients with advanced lung diseases often reach specialised centres at a stage when their respiratory function has deteriorated significantly. Through this dedicated clinic, our objective is to provide a structured approach to evaluating these patients, optimising their medical condition and counselling them and their families about available treatment options. A comprehensive and timely assessment can help identify suitable candidates before their condition progresses further and ensure that they receive appropriate care at every stage of their treatment journey.”

Mohit Singh, Regional Director, Fortis Hospital, Noida, said, “The launch of the Lung Failure Clinic reinforces Fortis Healthcare’s commitment to strengthening access to advanced and specialised respiratory care. Patients with end-stage lung diseases require a coordinated approach involving multiple medical specialties, supported by timely diagnosis, comprehensive evaluation and appropriate treatment pathways. Through this initiative, we aim to bring together clinical expertise and multidisciplinary capabilities to support patients with complex respiratory conditions and improve access to advanced treatment options, including lung transplantation.”

Dedicated Lung Failure Clinics are operational across several Fortis hospitals in Delhi/NCR.
